rationale: Both retained independent finals recommend exclusion, and their substantive conclusions agree with the supplied source and clause; there is no material disagreement to resolve. At exactly seven working days, the original calculation produces zero delay and zero payable penalty. The distinguishing fixture requirement concerns only an internal breach-day marker whose regulatory significance is unsupported. The proposed D5 boundary error therefore does not establish a regulatory defect. The separate calendar-day accrual concern remains unresolved and exceeds the allowed comparator locus.
scope_judgment: The allowed scope is solely CLOSPEN3.cbl line 30. Changing that boundary condition can affect branch execution at equality, but the demonstrated difference is an internal marker rather than payable penalty. This scope cannot establish calendar-day accrual or outstanding-dues eligibility.
intended_fixture_judgment: The equality fixture expects zero penalty, which the original source already computes, and a zero WS-SLA-BREACH-DAY instead of nine. Neither the clause nor any supplied downstream use establishes that zero-marker expectation as required regulatory behavior. Both reviewers correctly reject this fixture as evidence of the proposed regulatory defect.
regression_fixture_judgment: The six- and eight-working-day fixtures provide concrete observations strictly below and above the boundary, with expectations consistent with the original source. They support finite boundary coverage only. They do not demonstrate calendar-day delay across nonworking days, retained state on repeated invocation, outstanding-dues handling, or general preservation outside the locus. No execution results are supplied; these checks are not passes.
capability_judgment: The frozen backend identifies GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 and batch-executable support, making the paragraph fixtures executable in principle. It explicitly records that case checks have not been executed. Finite observation scope and incomplete static semantic-equivalence capability cannot establish general compliance or supply regulatory meaning for the marker.
duplicate_source_judgment: Preselection before detector results, continued grouping of repeated bundles as dependent, disclosure of case and distinct-bundle counts, and avoidance of independent-case interval claims provide a defensible procedural justification. The single-case packet cannot verify paired cases. Both retained reviewers exclude this case, so the stipulated all-reviewers-approve retention condition is unsatisfied. Dependence must remain disclosed.
